extracted.intended_audience: members of the mathematical community (AMS members, faculty, researchers, and mathematics educators)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcements and program descriptions summarizing eligibility, selection criteria, and desired outcomes for NSF grants/fellowships, MAA/AMS program nominations, and AMS employment-register scheduling priorities directed at the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Model Undergraduate Mathematical Sciences Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: MAA is searching for highly successful undergraduate mathematical sciences programs that (a) enhance recruitment and retention of mathematics majors; (b) prepare a substantial number of students effectively for teaching school mathematics or for continued graduate study; or (c) are particularly effective in attracting, and addressing the needs of, groups traditionally underrepresented in mathematics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MAA invites nominations (including self-nominations). Send nomination letters to Professor Alan C. Tucker, Applied Mathematics Department, SUNY-Stony Brook (email: atucker@sbccmail.bitnet). The search is funded by NSF to prepare case-study descriptions for the mathematical community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for Mathematical Preparation of Elementary School Teachers
rubrics_metrics.description: The report 'On the Mathematical Preparation of Elementary School Teachers' concludes more attention must be paid to what kind of mathematics elementary teachers learn, how they learn it, and how they bring their knowledge to actual classroom practice. Specific recommendations include a coordinated national effort to overhaul college mathematics for elementary teachers and adoption of a 12-semester-hour minimum for their mathematical preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional recommendations: create 'bridges' between colleges and elementary schools for continued professional development; establish institutes to improve teaching methods of college faculty who prepare teachers; professional societies (AMS and MAA) should explicitly recognize their critical role in preparing elementary teachers. The report is a short 17-page document and pointers to other standards (Professional Standards for Teaching Mathematics, Curriculum and Evaluation Standards for School Mathematics, Everybody Counts, A Call for Change) are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Calculus and Bridge to Calculus Program: proposal categories and desired outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF solicits proposals in three general categories: (1) projects to revitalize calculus instruction on a large scale involving collegiate and/or secondary students; (2) new curriculum development projects, particularly for the second year of calculus (including linear algebra and differential equations); (3) curriculum development projects focused on preparation for calculus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desired emphases for funded projects include raising student conceptual understanding, problem-solving and transfer skills; implementing methods that reduce tedious calculations and place the student in the role of an active learner. The program is managed by Division of Undergraduate Education in cooperation with other divisions. Closing date for proposals is December 7, 1992; references and examples of existing projects are noted (e.g., 'Priming the Calculus Pump'). Contacts: James Lightbourne at NSF (phone/email provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowship: eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are offered only to persons who (1) are citizens, nationals, or lawfully admitted permanent resident aliens of the United States as of January 1, 1993; (2) will have earned, by the beginning of their fellowship tenure, a doctoral degree in one of the mathematical sciences; (3) will have held the doctorate for no more than five years as of January 1, 1993; and (4) will not previously have held any other NSF postdoctoral fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards are for research in pure mathematics, applied mathematics and operations research, and statistics at appropriate nonprofit U.S. institutions. Subject to availability of funds, 30–40 awards expected in FY1993. Deadline for applications is October 15, 1992. Contacts: Office of Special Projects, Division of Mathematical Sciences, NSF, and AMS contact information are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Mathematical Sciences Postdoctoral Research Fellowship: evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of applicants will be based, in part, on ability as evidenced by past research work and letters of recommendation, likely impact on the future scientific development of the applicant, and the scientific quality of the research likely to emerge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications will be evaluated by a panel of mathematical scientists. Women, underrepresented minorities, and persons with disabilities are strongly encouraged to apply. Supporting contact emails and phone numbers are provided for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF Research at Foreign Centers: award scope and eligible hosts
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF's program for long-term research at foreign centers funds awards for research in any field of science or engineering supported by NSF for visits of three to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate foreign science and technology centers include industrial research laboratories, government research laboratories and centers, privately sponsored nonprofit institutions, and universities. Annual deadline for submissions is November 1. Contact: Division of International Programs, NSF (address and phone provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for Employment Register Interview Scheduling and Prioritization
rubrics_metrics.description: The enhanced interview scheduling system being developed will maintain the Employment Register tradition of maximizing the number of total interviews while supporting assignment of various levels of priority to certain classes of interview requests. One class assigned top priority are mutual requests (employer and applicant request each other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early tests indicate that virtually all mutual requests will be scheduled during the two days of the register. A full set of priorities and revised guidelines are being developed by the AMS–MAA–SIAM Joint Committee on Employment Opportunities. The October Notices will contain complete information including preregistration details.
